Same standard as evals/sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/macro-dsl-baseline.json and macro-dsl-skill.json for unchanged rules: git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/ leaves macros.md and library-design.md untouched, so the seven macro and library rules are graded as before. A route recorded by a direct attribute write inside get's quote counts against Keep quote blocks small, while validation in the macro body outside quote does not; the use documentation rule needs the effects of use in an admonition at the top of @moduledoc, and prose or nothing is violated; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them (Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden in all five runs); `unless` is listed under the branching rule, `if ... else` validation is not; a one-line multi-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; a catch-all public match clause or an unguarded match/1 is listed under Make polymorphism explicit; a format failure whose only change is parentheses on the two get calls is recorded as ok apart from locals_without_parens. The other SKILL.md changes since 0397dec (the When to load it and Reviewing code bullets, the defstruct sentence, Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call, Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order, the mix test sentence) touch no rule in macro-dsl's index list; no run defines a struct.

Changed rule, graded per sentence against its current text in idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md (Readability): Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else. Since 0397dec the wrapped-line sentence was rewritten to "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line: when `mix format` moves it onto a line of its own, the body is too long for `do:`, so write a block or move part of the body into a helper. The one wrap to keep is a head that `mix format` breaks after a long guard, with `do:` on the next line." and a sentence on `if` was added: "The same holds for `if`: `if ..., do: ..., else: ...` fits when each branch is one short expression on the `if`'s line, and a branch `mix format` moves onto its own line gets `do ... end`." Violating runs per sentence, out of five: "Use `do:` for a body of one expression that reads as part of the head": 0 (every one-expression block clause was joined into a do: line and measured; all are 100 to 193 characters, so each block is needed). "A body with several steps, a `case` or `with`, or a comment gets `do ... end`.": 0 (no do: body holds a pipeline, case or with; opus-1's two-step match/1 pipeline at lines 81-83 is a block). "A function whose clauses are short pattern matches keeps them on `do:` even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line.": 0 (haiku-1 bind/3 and haiku-2 match_segments/3 keep their short clauses on do: and set the block clauses apart). "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks.": 1, opus-1, whose validate_path!/2 keeps line 94 `defp validate_path!("/" <> _ = path, _env), do: path` on do: while its other two clauses (lines 96 and 100) need blocks (137 and 127 characters as do: lines), the shape that broke skill-sonnet-1 in 2026-10-22-b. "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line ...": 3, haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2. No run's file has a do: body on a line of its own (grep for lines starting with do: or else: finds none), because none of the sessions ran mix format; mix format on copies moves three do: bodies onto their own lines: haiku-1 line 75 `defp bind([literal | pattern], [literal | segments], params), do: bind(pattern, segments, params)` (99 characters) becomes `defp bind([literal | pattern], [literal | segments], params),` / `do: bind(pattern, segments, params)`; sonnet-1 line 48 `defp do_match(unquote(pattern)), do: {:ok, unquote(handler), %{unquote_splicing(params)}}` (99 characters, inside the quote) becomes `defp do_match(unquote(pattern)),` / `do: {:ok, unquote(handler), %{unquote_splicing(params)}}`; sonnet-2 line 46 `defp do_match(unquote(pattern)), do: {:ok, unquote(handler), unquote({:%{}, [], params})}` (99 characters, inside the quote) becomes `defp do_match(unquote(pattern)),` / `do: {:ok, unquote(handler), unquote({:%{}, [], params})}`. None of the three heads has a guard, so none is the guard wrap the rule keeps. "The one wrap to keep ...": not exercised; no head in any run has a guard long enough for mix format to break it. "The same holds for `if` ...": 0; every if and unless in the five runs (opus-1 lines 107, 124, 136; haiku-1 lines 28, 32; sonnet-1 lines 82, 88; sonnet-2 lines 81, 98) is a block whose do: form would run past 98 characters, and no run writes `if ..., do:`. Any sentence: 4 of 5 (opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), so all three tiers are violated (2026-10-22-b baseline: Opus clean, Haiku violated, Sonnet violated).

Compile-time dependencies were checked with mix xref trace in scratch Mix projects, one per run, with the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex (so xref line numbers match the run file) and real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/my_app/handlers.ex. Every run reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile) and alias MyApp.UserHandler (compile) on the two get lines. haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 call Macro.expand on the handler; opus-1 calls Macro.expand_literals(handler_ast, env) with env = __CALLER__ unchanged, whose function is nil in the module body, so the expansion is still a compile-time reference; the rule's example sets function: in the env.

Bad-declaration checks: each run's project was loaded, then Code.compile_string compiled one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one declaring get "/", "not a module". All ten fail while get expands in the router module: CompileError in opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2, ArgumentError in sonnet-1.

Format: mix format on copies adds parentheses to the two get calls in all five runs (result.json format_ok is false for that reason); it also reflows opus-1 line 127, haiku-1 lines 33 and 75, sonnet-1 line 48 and sonnet-2 line 46, which are listed under Before you finish (and the three do: lines under the do: rule). haiku-2's only change is the get parentheses. All five compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors.

Reads: result.json reads is empty for all five runs; the transcripts never mention SKILL.md, macros.md or library-design.md and make no Skill call, as the baseline prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") asks. The Expected reads line is missed by design in every run.

Smoke test outside the rules: all five return the routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", and return :error for "/nope". haiku-2 returns atom param keys (%{id: "42"}) built with String.to_atom from the route string, which is source code, not external input, so it is not counted under the atom rule; the others return string keys. match(123) raises FunctionClauseError in the generated match/1 in opus-1 and haiku-1, raises FunctionClauseError in String.split/3 in haiku-2 (unguarded match/1), and returns :error in sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 (catch-all clauses).

Against 2026-10-22-b baseline: opus-1 again writes the route attribute directly in get's quote and again makes handlers compile-time dependencies, now through Macro.expand_literals without a function in the env instead of Macro.expand; unlike that sweep's opus-1 it leaves the generated routes/0 and match/1 without @spec, so the opus tier moves from clean to violated on the spec rule, and its three-clause validate_path!/2 moves the opus tier from clean to violated on the do: rule. Every run this sweep again has the direct-attribute-write shape, no admonition, and compile-time handler dependencies; Write a function unless the job needs a macro, Unquote each argument once and Write module names literally stay clean in all five.
